description: The Survey and Diary of Consumer Payment Choice (SDCPC) gives a picture of US consumers' payment preferences and behaviour, combining a survey with a three-day payment diary that records each transaction. For 2025 it found consumers made an average of 47 payments a month, about one fewer than in October 2024, worth 6,656 dollars against 6,867 dollars. It is produced by the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, with Kevin Foster as survey director and Marcin Hitczenko as co-author of the June 2026 report. Coverage is the United States. The report, tables with standard errors and public use data sets at day, individual and transaction level are available free in CSV, Stata and R formats, with a codebook, questionnaires and weighting information. Caveats: diaries cover only three days per respondent, results depend on survey weights, and the page read gives no licence. For simulation it provides transaction-level data on how people pay, needed to model the effect of a card network, payment system or cash distribution outage on households and merchants. It is related to the ECB payments statistics record in this catalogue, a euro area payments source.
